equation_request.abstract: We show that any unitary operator on the $d_{A}\times d_{B}$ system ($d_{A}\geq 2$) can be decomposed into the product of at most $4d_{A}-5$ controlled unitary operators. The number can be reduced to $2d_{A}-1$ when $d_{A}$ is a power of two. We also prove that three controlled unitaries can implement a bipartite complex permutation operator, and discuss the connection to an analogous result on classical reversible circuits. We further show that any $n$-partite unitary on the space $\mathbb{C}^{d_{1}}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathbb{C}^{d_{n}}$ is the product of at most $[2\prod^{n-1}_{j=1}(2d_{j}-2)-1]$ controlled unitary gates, each of which is controlled from $n-1$ systems. We also decompose any bipartite unitary into the product of a simple type of bipartite gates and some local unitaries. We derive dimension-independent upper bounds for the CNOT-gate cost or entanglement cost of bipartite permutation unitaries (with the help of ancillas of fixed size) as functions of the Schmidt rank of the unitary. It is shown that such costs under a simple protocol are related to the log-rank conjecture in communication complexity theory via the link of nonnegative rank.

specification.problem: Characterize how many controlled unitaries are needed to decompose an arbitrary bipartite (d_A x d_B) or n-partite unitary, and bound CNOT or entanglement cost of bipartite permutation unitaries in terms of Schmidt rank, including a link to the log-rank conjecture via nonnegative rank.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level statement of decomposition bounds only; no explicit circuits, constructions, or proofs are reconstructed. Equations capture only the stated counting bounds on controlled unitaries.

specification.initial_state: Arbitrary input state on A and B; the decomposition is operator-level and does not fix a state.

steps.description: Take an arbitrary target unitary U on A⊗B.
Write U as a product of at most 4d_A-5 controlled unitaries, controlled on A and acting on B (alternating control roles may be used; the exact construction is not given in the abstract).
If d_A is a power of two, the product length reduces to at most 2d_A-1.
For n parties, use at most the stated number of gates, each controlled from n-1 systems.

specification.measurement: None prescribed: the result is an operator-level decomposition. Any verification would compare the product of controlled unitaries with the target U, for example via process fidelity or by checking action on a basis, but the abstract gives no measurement.
specification.classical_postprocessing: None given in the abstract. Classical computation would be needed to find the controlled-unitary factors, but the method is not stated.
